1.explanation: To introduce a `--light` modifier, we must update both the vanilla‐JS and React implementations. In the config file (overflow-menu.config.js) we need a new ‘light’ variant in the `variants` array so Storybook and the CSS generator include it. In the vanilla component (overflow-menu.js) the static `options` getter holds class names (e.g. `classMenuShown`, `classShown`), so it must be extended to recognize and apply a `--light` class; the `getMenuOffset` function will need no change for contrast but should be aware if positioning differs for light styling (if any). In the React component (OverflowMenu.js), its exported `getMenuOffset` should accept an extra `light` flag if needed, and the `render` method must read a new `light` prop, add the `${prefix}--overflow-menu--light` class to its root element, and reflect that in its PropTypes and defaultProps so users can enable the light style via `<OverflowMenu light>`.
1.bug_scenario: The OverflowMenu is rendering in a medium‐gray style against a light‐gray page background, making the menu blend in and lose contrast. The user wants a “light” version (e.g. a `--light` modifier) so that the menu background can switch to white (or a lighter shade) when placed on gray pages. The attached screenshot shows a gray menu on a gray container, which is hard to distinguish.

2.explanation:
• overflow-menu.config.js: the Storybook variants list currently only defines “default” and “up”; a new “light” variant should be added here (with `context.light = true`) so that the light modifier is applied in the static demos.
• OverflowMenu (React) class: needs a new boolean `light` prop (in static propTypes/defaultProps) and the render() method must detect `this.props.light` and append the CSS class `${settings.prefix}--overflow-menu--light` alongside the existing flavour classes.
• OverflowMenuExample in the story file: the story definition should include a knob or a new story entry to toggle or display the light version — wiring the `light` prop through to the component so designers can preview and test the high-contrast style.
